title: Close the class, not the instance
statement: Treat each defect, finding or failure as a class: repair its kind and add a standing check across everything made the same way, not just the items that failed.
example: 39 checks were added in 5 weeks, yet one defect class took seven separate commits.
detail: The reading project's QA notes found that 39 checks were added in 5 weeks (7-10 a week) while the same defect classes kept coming back, one of them across seven separate commits, and a later formatting commit silently reverted an earlier pronunciation fix. What converged was closing a finding only when its whole class has an executable check of what the student experiences, and counting new against repeat classes in every round report. When one instance of a text-to-speech trap turned up, the rule became a census of every instance in the course file rather than assuming a one-off, and a give-away cue rule was swept over every grade. Where code can't check a class, a dated rule stands in for the check, and each check is shown to fire before the fix and runs on every lesson.
against: A class-level check can reach too far: one specified rule was kept unwired because both of its candidate forms flagged approved, reviewed content. The same roadmap found one complaint class counted as machine-catchable covered only by a lint on one word family, not the length the complaint was about, so a class check has to be shown to cover its class (`grade3-reading/artifacts/cert-layer/AUTOMATED-CHECKS-ROADMAP-2026-08-31.md`). Some renders voice such an opening anyway, so each case's transcript is checked rather than assumed (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0200-content-audio-review-traps.qmd`). A class check has to be precise before it is wired in: one rule for where a question belongs was specified but kept unwired, because both of its candidate forms flagged approved, reviewed content (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0234-misc-artifacts-gate-eval-checks-recovery.qmd`, lines 83-85). The set catches only mistakes that have been named at least once, so content that can fail in new ways still needs people's judgment (shadow-bench/docs/brainlift.md line 143), and '*Weakest point:* learning only from refusals means approvals teach nothing.' (line 118). The same document records the objection that 'a pile of prohibitions has no construct validity, so content can pass every check and still teach badly' (line 108). The standard that states it is a draft that binds nobody, and the test it names for the practice, findings per lesson falling round by round, has no recorded result in that file (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0217-team-direction-2026-09-09.qmd`). The standard was a draft, not shared or adopted, that binds nobody (`grade3-reading/artifacts/team-direction-2026-09-09/GATE-STANDARD-DRAFT.md`). Some repairs held on fresh rows: single-shot runs on rows 100-149 gave "239/250 = 95.6%" (aptraining-local/den-of-ideation/reports/validation_triage/20260524T202325Z_2026-05-24T2022Z_UNIT1_LEQ_SOLVER_v3_VALIDATED_99_6pct.md.md, line 140). One of the new failures, row 27, was a "timeout/null rating" rather than a graded miss (aptraining-local/den-of-ideation/reports/unit1_leq_solver_v3_final_gap_repair_delivery_20260524T1840Z.md, line 11). A later run found counter-evidence (`grade3-reading/curriculum-gen/.agent/AGENT.md`). A later run found counter-evidence (`grade3-reading/artifacts/arc-audit/REGISTER-2026-09-15.md`).

Today: **qa-must-converge** — rounds fixed instances and shipped incident-shaped checks (39 checks in 5 weeks, 7–10 a week) while the CLASSES recurred (glow/scroll fixed 09-03, 09-04, 09-07, 09-14; silent audio seven commits 08-26→09-14). Going forward: experience invariants over mechanism assertions; a detector for every safety rule that degrades to silence; a recurrence gauge per round (new classes vs repeats); human QA on a frozen staging after waves, not during; a finding closes when its class has an executable invariant, not when the item is fixed.

**Reviewer feedback is scoped to its own course.** A matching string elsewhere is not a ruling.

**A repeat-offense item is a process failure, not a content failure.** The moment a reviewer gives the same feedback a second time, the CLASS gets a red-controlled validator the same day — a third occurrence must be structurally impossible.
